family.name: IT Support / Helpdesk
family.summary: Monday 9 am: a phishing email someone typed their password into, a VPN outage and the CEO’s board meeting. Triage it, contain the phishing, and catch the hole in the password reset process.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Monday 9 am
stages.summary: Order a queue with a security incident, an outage for remote staff and the CEO's deadline. Think aloud.

stages.title: The phishing email
stages.summary: Choose how to respond to a phishing incident with one password entered. Think aloud.

stages.title: An hour later
stages.summary: What their response led to. Tests adapting during an incident.

stages.title: Review the password reset process
stages.summary: A phone reset process that verifies people with public information and reads passwords aloud. Think aloud.

stages.title: VPN outage update (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the staff update about the VPN outage with AI. Catches jargon and invented fix times.

stages.title: An incident you handled
stages.summary: A real outage or security problem they handled. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You're on the IT support team at **Greenleaf Pharma**, a pharmaceutical distributor with 256 staff. There are two of you today; your colleague is at the other office until noon. It's 9 am on Monday.

brief.caption: Open tickets
rows: Laptop is "very slow" since last week.
Please install a screen recording tool.
A new joiner started today and can't log in to anything.
Printer on floor 2 is jammed again.
VPN won't connect for anyone working from home since 8:30 am.
"Got an email from 'HR' about a salary revision with a login link. I clicked it and entered my password, then got suspicious." (Others say they clicked but didn't log in.)
The CEO's laptop won't show on the boardroom screen. Board meeting starts in 40 minutes.

brief.text: The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: Tell us about a tech problem you solved at home or for family.
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **What do you do in the next hour, in what order, and why?** Use the ticket numbers. Say what can wait until your colleague is back.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

choices.label: Reset the affected accounts, check their mailboxes and block the sender
Force a password reset for the whole company now
Send a company-wide warning email and watch
Wait for the security vendor, who responds in four hours

prompt.text: 4 people reported the email; one entered their password, 2 others clicked the link. You don't know how many others received it. **How do you respond?** Pick one, then list your first five actions.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Reset the affected accounts, check their mailboxes and block the sender"

prompt.text: In the compromised mailbox you find a rule forwarding every email containing "invoice" to accounts-team@out1ook-mail.com, created at 7:12 am. Finance says a supplier emailed new bank details this morning.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Force a password reset for the whole company now"

prompt.text: 32 people are locked out and calling. The board meeting has started without the CEO's slides. You haven't yet looked at the compromised mailbox.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Send a company-wide warning email and watch"

prompt.text: After the warning, two more people say they entered their passwords last week. And the compromised account has sent the same phishing email to Greenleaf Pharma's clients.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Wait for the security vendor, who responds in four hours"

prompt.text: While you waited, the compromised account sent the phishing email to the whole company and to clients. The vendor's first response is "please send us the logs".
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: Your manager asks you to review the current phone process for password resets. **Name the problems, worst first, and how each could be abused.** Then write the process you would use instead.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

items: Caller gives their full name and employee ID.
If they match the directory, reset the password to Welcome@123 and read it out on the call.
Tell them to change it "when they get a chance".
For senior staff, skip the checks if the caller sounds stressed and says it is urgent.
Log the ticket number in the helpdesk tool.

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.
Write the message to the 55 remote staff (under 100 words): what's happening, what they can do meanwhile, and when they'll hear next. You don't yet know the cause.

items: Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Tell us about an outage or security problem you had to handle.** What did you see, what did you do, and what would you do differently?
Specifics such as numbers and timelines matter more than polish.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.
